# Configuration options

Every key below can be set in `config.json` or as the environment variable
next to it. Environment variables win over the file. Nested keys are written with
dots: `runner.executor.type` is `{"runner": {"executor": {"type": ...}}}`.

This page is generated from the JEH source, so it always matches the
release it ships with. For how to supply these options, see
[Configuration](../configuration.md).

<a id="database"></a>

## Database

JEH creates and migrates its own tables on start. Pick the dialect before the first run; changing it later means migrating the data yourself.

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mysql.host`<br />`JEH_DB_HOST` | string<br />Default: `0.0.0.0` | MySQL database host. |
| `mysql.user`<br />`JEH_DB_USER` | string | MySQL user name. |
| `mysql.pass`<br />`JEH_DB_PASS` | string | Password of the database user. Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |
| `mysql.name`<br />`JEH_DB` | string<br />Default: `jeh` | MySQL database (schema) name. |
| `mysql.options`<br />`JEH_DB_OPTIONS` | object | Extra driver options appended to the DSN, as a JSON object of name/value pairs. |
| `postgres.host`<br />`JEH_DB_HOST` | string<br />Default: `0.0.0.0` | Postgres database host. |
| `postgres.user`<br />`JEH_DB_USER` | string | Postgres user name. |
| `postgres.pass`<br />`JEH_DB_PASS` | string | Password of the database user. Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |
| `postgres.name`<br />`JEH_DB` | string<br />Default: `jeh` | Postgres database (schema) name. |
| `postgres.options`<br />`JEH_DB_OPTIONS` | object | Extra driver options appended to the connection string, as a JSON object of name/value pairs. Use it for `sslmode`, for example. |
| `sqlite.host`<br />`JEH_DB_HOST` | string<br />Default: `0.0.0.0` | Path to the SQLite database file. |
| `sqlite.user`<br />`JEH_DB_USER` | string | Unused for SQLite. The database is a file and needs no credentials. |
| `sqlite.pass`<br />`JEH_DB_PASS` | string | Unused for SQLite. The database is a file and needs no credentials. Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |
| `sqlite.name`<br />`JEH_DB` | string<br />Default: `jeh` | Path to the SQLite database file. |
| `sqlite.options`<br />`JEH_DB_OPTIONS` | object | Extra driver options appended to the DSN, as a JSON object of name/value pairs. |
| `dialect`<br />`JEH_DB_DIALECT` | string<br />Default: `sqlite` | Database engine JEH stores its data in. One of `mysql`, `postgres`, `sqlite`. |

<a id="web-server"></a>

## Web server

Where the HTTP server listens and how users reach it. Set `web_host` to the URL users type: redirect URIs, webhook targets, and links in notifications are built from it.

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `port`<br />`JEH_PORT` | string<br />Default: `:3000` | Format `:port_num` eg, :3000 if : is missing it will be corrected |
| `tls.enabled`<br />`JEH_TLS_ENABLED` | boolean | Enable or disable TLS (HTTPS) for secure communication with the JEH server. |
| `tls.cert_file`<br />`JEH_TLS_CERT_FILE` | string | Path to TLS certificate file. |
| `tls.key_file`<br />`JEH_TLS_KEY_FILE` | string | Path to TLS key file. |
| `tls.http_redirect_addr`<br />`JEH_TLS_HTTP_REDIRECT_ADDR` | string | Address (`host[:port]`) for the HTTP→HTTPS redirect listener. Mutually exclusive with `tls.http_redirect_port`. |
| `tls.http_redirect_port`<br />`JEH_TLS_HTTP_REDIRECT_PORT` | integer | Port to redirect HTTP traffic to HTTPS. Mutually exclusive with `tls.http_redirect_addr`. |
| `interface`<br />`JEH_INTERFACE` | string | Ip, put in front of the port. defaults to empty |
| `web_host`<br />`JEH_WEB_ROOT` | string | web host |
| `cookie_hash`<br />`JEH_COOKIE_HASH` | string | cookie hashing & encryption Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |
| `cookie_encryption`<br />`JEH_COOKIE_ENCRYPTION` | string | BASE64-encoded key used to encrypt session cookies. Generate with `head -c32 /dev/urandom \| base64`. Changing it signs every user out. Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |

<a id="paths-and-storage"></a>

## Paths and storage

Directories JEH writes to. Everything here except the database is a cache that can be recreated.

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `tmp_path`<br />`JEH_TMP_PATH` | string<br />Default: `/tmp/jeh` | jeh stores ephemeral projects here |
| `secrets_path`<br />`JEH_SECRETS_PATH` | string | Legacy top-level setting for backwards compatibility. Users should prefer configuring dirs.secrets instead. |
| `home_dir_mode`<br />`JEH_HOME_DIR_MODE` | string<br />Default: `template_dir` | Controls how the HOME environment variable is set for tasks. "template_home" (default) — HOME is set to a per-template directory, isolating .ansible/ across parallel tasks. Repo is cloned into a "src" subdirectory under HOME. "project_home" — HOME is set to the project temp directory (legacy behavior). Parallel ansible-galaxy runs in the same project may conflict. "user_home" — HOME is not overridden (keeps the real user HOME). ANSIBLE_HOME is set per template to isolate .ansible/ for Ansible tasks. One of `user_home`, `project_home`, `template_dir`. |
| `dirs.secrets`<br />`JEH_SECRETS_PATH` | string<br />Default: `/tmp/jeh` | Path to directory where secrets are stored (for example Vault token files). Default: `/tmp/jeh`. Legacy top-level `secrets_path` is still accepted when `dirs.secrets` is unset or left at the default. |
| `dirs.repos`<br />`JEH_REPOS_DIR` | string | Path to directory where repositories are stored. |
| `dirs.ssh_agent_sockets`<br />`JEH_SSH_AGENT_SOCKETS_DIR` | string<br />Default: `/tmp/jeh` | Path to directory where SSH agent sockets are stored. Default: /tmp/jeh |

<a id="encryption"></a>

## Encryption

Keys that protect stored secrets. Back them up separately from the database: the database is unreadable without them.

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `access_key_encryption`<br />`JEH_ACCESS_KEY_ENCRYPTION` | string | BASE64 encoded byte array used for encrypting and decrypting access keys stored in database. Legacy entry point kept for backward compatibility; the access keyring is configured via EncryptionKeys.AccessKey (encryption_keys.access_key). Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |
| `option_encryption`<br />`JEH_OPTION_ENCRYPTION` | string | BASE64 encoded key used to encrypt/decrypt DB options (the JWT signing key) with the old single-key scheme (no rotation). It is the option-keyring counterpart of AccessKeyEncryption: when set the option keyring uses this one key; rotation is configured instead via the keys file (encryption.keys_file → option_key). When unset, options fall back to the access keyring. Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |
| `encryption.keys_file`<br />`JEH_ENCRYPTION_KEYS_FILE` | string | Path to the EncryptionKeysConfig file (the keyrings). |
| `encryption.keys_poll_interval`<br />`JEH_ENCRYPTION_KEYS_POLL_INTERVAL` | string<br />Default: `15s` | How often the keys file is checked for changes (a Go duration like "15s"). "0" disables polling (SIGHUP still forces a reload). |

<a id="authentication"></a>

## Authentication

How users sign in. See [Authentication](../configuration.md) for the provider-side setup.

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `auth.max_session_life_hours`<br />`JEH_AUTH_MAX_SESSION_LIFE_HOURS` | integer | Absolute lifetime of a login session in hours, counted from the moment the user logged in. Once exceeded the session is rejected and expired, even if it was active recently, and the user must log in again. 0 (default) means no absolute limit: sessions then only expire after SessionInactivityTimeout without activity. |
| `mfa.totp.enabled`<br />`JEH_TOTP_ENABLED` | boolean | Enable Two-factor authentication using TOTP. |
| `mfa.totp.allow_recovery`<br />`JEH_TOTP_ALLOW_RECOVERY` | boolean | Allow users to reset TOTP using a recovery code. |
| `mfa.totp.app_name`<br />`JEH_TOTP_ISSUER` | string | Issuer label (JEH title) shown in TOTP authenticator apps. |
| `mfa.email.enabled`<br />`JEH_EMAIL_2TP_ENABLED` | boolean | Enable email-based multi-factor authentication. |
| `mfa.email.allow_login_as_external_user`<br />`JEH_EMAIL_2TP_ALLOW_LOGIN_AS_EXTERNAL_USER` | boolean | Allow login as an external (email-only) user. |
| `mfa.email.allow_create_external_user`<br />`JEH_EMAIL_2TP_ALLOW_CREATE_EXTERNAL_USER` | boolean | Allow creating external users on first login. |
| `mfa.email.allowed_domains`<br />`JEH_EMAIL_2TP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` | array | JSON array of allowed email domains. |
| `mfa.email.disable_for_oidc`<br />`JEH_EMAIL_2TP_DISABLE_FOR_OIDC` | boolean | Disable email MFA for users authenticated via OIDC. |
| `ldap_enable`<br />`JEH_LDAP_ENABLE` | boolean | Turns on the legacy single-directory LDAP login configured by the flat ldap_* settings below. Use ldap_providers instead when more than one directory is involved. |
| `ldap_binddn`<br />`JEH_LDAP_BIND_DN` | string | The distinguished name (DN) used to bind to the LDAP server for authentication. |
| `ldap_bindpassword`<br />`JEH_LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD` | string | Password of the bind account used to search the directory. Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |
| `ldap_server`<br />`JEH_LDAP_SERVER` | string | The hostname and port of the LDAP server (e.g., ldap-server.com:1389). |
| `ldap_searchdn`<br />`JEH_LDAP_SEARCH_DN` | string | The base distinguished name (DN) used for searching users in the LDAP directory (e.g., dc=example,dc=org). |
| `ldap_searchfilter`<br />`JEH_LDAP_SEARCH_FILTER` | string | The filter used to search for users in the LDAP directory (e.g., (&(objectClass=inetOrgPerson)(uid=%s))). |
| `ldap_mappings.dn`<br />`JEH_LDAP_MAPPING_DN` | string<br />Default: `dn` | LDAP attribute to use as the distinguished name (DN) mapping for user authentication. |
| `ldap_mappings.mail`<br />`JEH_LDAP_MAPPING_MAIL` | string<br />Default: `mail` | LDAP attribute to use as the email address mapping for user authentication. |
| `ldap_mappings.uid`<br />`JEH_LDAP_MAPPING_UID` | string<br />Default: `uid` | LDAP attribute to use as the user ID (UID) mapping for user authentication. |
| `ldap_mappings.cn`<br />`JEH_LDAP_MAPPING_CN` | string<br />Default: `cn` | LDAP attribute to use as the common name (CN) mapping for user authentication. |
| `ldap_needtls`<br />`JEH_LDAP_NEEDTLS` | boolean | Flag to enable or disable TLS for LDAP connections. |
| `ldap_tls_skip_verify`<br />`JEH_LDAP_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY` | boolean | Disables verification of the LDAP server's TLS certificate for the legacy flat ldap_* config. Defaults to false (certificates are verified). See LdapProvider.TLSSkipVerify. |
| `ldap_providers`<br />`JEH_LDAP_PROVIDERS` | object | Configures multiple LDAP directories (like OidcProviders for OIDC). The key is the provider ID shown in identity records; the ID "ldap" is reserved for the legacy flat ldap_* config above. |
| `oidc_providers`<br />`JEH_OIDC_PROVIDERS` | object | Configures OpenID Connect sign-in. The key is the provider ID that appears in identity records and in the /auth/oidc/\<id>/login URL, so it must stay stable once users have signed in through it. |
| `password_login_disable`<br />`JEH_PASSWORD_LOGIN_DISABLED` | boolean | Rejects the "password" login method, leaving LDAP and OpenID Connect as the only ways in. Set it once an identity provider is configured and working, so that local passwords stop being a second door. |
| `external_auth_email_matching`<br />`JEH_EXTERNAL_AUTH_EMAIL_MATCHING` | string<br />Default: `auto` | Controls whether an LDAP/OIDC login may be linked to an existing user by email when no external identity record exists yet: "auto" (default) - only external users without any linked identity (one-time adoption of pre-2.20 accounts); "always" - any external user (needed when the same person logs in via several providers); "never" - identities are matched strictly by provider ID. Local (password) accounts are never matched regardless of the mode. One of `auto`, `always`, `never`. |
| `non_admin_can_create_project`<br />`JEH_NON_ADMIN_CAN_CREATE_PROJECT` | boolean | Allow non-admin users to create projects. |

<a id="git"></a>

## Git

How repositories are cloned. See [Repositories](../configuration.md).

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ssh_config_path`<br />`JEH_SSH_PATH` | string | Path to the custom SSH config file. Default path is ~/.ssh/config. |
| `ssh.config_path`<br />`JEH_SSH_PATH` | string | SshConfigPath is a path to the custom SSH config file. Default path is ~/.ssh/config. |
| `ssh.known_hosts_file`<br />`JEH_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_FILE` | string | SshKnownHostsFile is a path to the SSH known_hosts file used to verify git server host keys. When set, host-key checking is strict: a key that is missing from (or changed relative to) this file aborts the connection, preventing a network attacker from impersonating the git server. When empty, JEH uses a persistent trust-on-first-use file under TmpPath (StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new): the first connection to a host is trusted and pinned, and any later host-key change is rejected. |
| `ssh.strict_host_key_checking` | string<br />Default: `no` | Host key policy for git over SSH: `no` accepts any key, `yes` requires the key to be in the known_hosts file already, `accept-new` pins the key on first connection and rejects later changes. |
| `git_client`<br />`JEH_GIT_CLIENT` | string<br />Default: `cmd_git` | Implementation used to clone repositories: `cmd_git` shells out to the installed `git`, `go_git` uses the built-in Go library. One of `go_git`, `cmd_git`. |
| `git_submodule_jobs`<br />`JEH_GIT_SUBMODULE_JOBS` | integer<br />Default: `4` | How many submodules the command-line Git client fetches in parallel during clone and update operations. |
| `git_attempts`<br />`JEH_GIT_ATTEMPTS` | integer<br />Default: `4` | How many times a git clone or pull is tried before the task fails, for git servers which are intermittently unavailable. 1 tries once and does not retry. |

<a id="tasks"></a>

## Tasks

Concurrency, retention, and the environment task processes run in.

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `max_task_duration_sec`<br />`JEH_MAX_TASK_DURATION_SEC` | integer | Max duration of a task in seconds. |
| `max_tasks_per_template`<br />`JEH_MAX_TASKS_PER_TEMPLATE` | integer | Maximum number of recent tasks stored in the database for each template. |
| `max_parallel_tasks`<br />`JEH_MAX_PARALLEL_TASKS` | integer<br />Default: `9999` | task concurrency |
| `apps`<br />`JEH_APPS` | object | JSON map which contains apps configuration. |
| `env_vars`<br />`JEH_ENV_VARS` | object | JSON map which contains environment variables exposed to task runs. |
| `forwarded_env_vars`<br />`JEH_FORWARDED_ENV_VARS` | array | Lists host environment variables copied into task runs and into the child git processes that clone and update repositories. Proxy variables are not forwarded implicitly: they reach a task only if they are named here or set in env_vars. A bare-metal (systemd) installation behind a corporate proxy therefore has to list the proxy variables explicitly, including the bypass list for internal hosts: ["HTTP_PROXY", "HTTPS_PROXY", "NO_PROXY"]. |
| `process.user`<br />`JEH_PROCESS_USER` | string | User under which wrapped processes (such as Ansible, Terraform, or OpenTofu) will run. |
| `process.uid`<br />`JEH_PROCESS_UID` | integer | ID of user under which wrapped processes (such as Ansible, Terraform, or OpenTofu) will run. |
| `process.chroot`<br />`JEH_PROCESS_CHROOT` | string | Chroot directory for wrapped processes. |
| `process.gid`<br />`JEH_PROCESS_GID` | integer | ID for group under which wrapped processes (such as Ansible, Terraform, or OpenTofu) will run. |
| `process.no_new_privs`<br />`JEH_PROCESS_NO_NEW_PRIVS` | boolean | Set the `no_new_privs` flag so wrapped processes cannot gain new privileges. |
| `process.app_namespaces.user`<br />`JEH_PROCESS_APP_NS_USER` | boolean | Isolates UIDs/GIDs (CLONE_NEWUSER). Enables unprivileged use of the other namespaces. |
| `process.app_namespaces.mount`<br />`JEH_PROCESS_APP_NS_MOUNT` | boolean | Hides host mount points such as secret tmpfs (CLONE_NEWNS). |
| `process.app_namespaces.pid`<br />`JEH_PROCESS_APP_NS_PID` | boolean | Hides host processes from child apps (CLONE_NEWPID). |
| `process.app_namespaces.ipc`<br />`JEH_PROCESS_APP_NS_IPC` | boolean | Isolates SysV IPC and POSIX message queues (CLONE_NEWIPC). |
| `process.app_namespaces.uts`<br />`JEH_PROCESS_APP_NS_UTS` | boolean | Isolates hostname and domain (CLONE_NEWUTS). |
| `schedule.timezone`<br />`JEH_SCHEDULE_TIMEZONE` | string<br />Default: `UTC` | Timezone used for scheduling tasks and cron jobs. Default: UTC |

<a id="runners"></a>

## Runners

Server-side switches first, then the keys a runner reads from its own configuration file. See [Runners](../configuration.md).

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `runner_registration_token`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_REGISTRATION_TOKEN` | string | Deprecated, use Runners field instead of it. |
| `use_remote_runner`<br />`JEH_USE_REMOTE_RUNNER` | boolean | Deprecated. Use Runners field instead of it. |
| `runner.registration_token_file`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_REGISTRATION_TOKEN_FILE` | string | Path to file containing the runner registration token. |
| `runner.token`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_TOKEN` | string | Authentication token this runner presents to the server. Issued by `jeh runner register`. Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |
| `runner.token_file`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_TOKEN_FILE` | string | Path to token file for runner registration. |
| `runner.one_off`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_ONE_OFF` | boolean | Indicates than runner runs only one job and exit. It is very useful for dynamic runners. How it works? Example: 1) User starts the task. 2) JEH found runner for task and calls runner's webhook if it provided. 3) Your server or lambda handling the call and starts the one-off runner. 4) The runner connects to the JEH server and handles the enqueued task(s). |
| `runner.enabled`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_ENABLED` | boolean | Enable the runner. |
| `runner.webhook`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_WEBHOOK` | string | Webhook URL for runner. |
| `runner.name`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_NAME` | string | Runner name. |
| `runner.tags`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_TAGS` | array | JSON array of runner tags. |
| `runner.max_parallel_tasks`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_MAX_PARALLEL_TASKS` | integer<br />Default: `9999` | Max number of parallel tasks for the runner. Default: 9999. |
| `runner.project_id`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_PROJECT_ID` | integer | Restrict the runner to a single project. |
| `runner.check_interval_seconds`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | integer<br />Default: `1` | How often the runner polls the server for new jobs. Plain int, not time.Duration, for env-binding simplicity. |
| `runner.connection.server_ca_cert_file`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_SERVER_CA_CERT_FILE` | string | PEM bundle used to verify the JEH server's certificate, in addition to the system trust store. Set this when the server uses a self-signed or internal-CA cert. |
| `runner.connection.skip_tls_verify`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_SKIP_TLS_VERIFY` | boolean | Disables server certificate verification entirely. This is insecure (vulnerable to MITM) — use only for testing. |
| `runner.executor`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_EXECUTOR` | object | The whole executor block as one JSON value, for deployments that configure the runner entirely through environment variables. Equivalent to setting the nested `runner.executor.*` keys. |
| `runner.executor.type`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_EXECUTOR_TYPE` | string<br />Default: `local` | Strategy the runner uses to execute each task: `local` (default), `k8s` or `docker`. |
| `runner.executor.k8s.kubeconfig` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_K8S_KUBECONFIG` | string | Path to a kubeconfig file. When empty, in-cluster configuration is used (ServiceAccount token + CA cert mounted by Kubernetes). |
| `runner.executor.k8s.namespace` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_K8S_NAMESPACE` | string<br />Default: `jeh` | Where ephemeral task Pods are created. |
| `runner.executor.k8s.image` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_K8S_IMAGE` | string<br />Default: `impishmd/jeh:latest-job` | Default container image used for the build container of each task Pod. Templates may override this in a future phase. |
| `runner.executor.k8s.helper_image` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_K8S_HELPER_IMAGE` | string<br />Default: `impishmd/jeh:latest-helper` | Image used for the git-clone init container (Phase 3+). |
| `runner.executor.k8s.service_account` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_K8S_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` | string<br />Default: `default` | That task Pods run under. Defaults to the namespace's default SA. |
| `runner.executor.k8s.pull_secrets` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_K8S_PULL_SECRETS` | string | Comma-separated list of imagePullSecrets attached to each Pod. |
| `runner.executor.k8s.poll_interval_seconds` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_K8S_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | integer<br />Default: `3` | Controls how often the executor polls Pod status. Defaults to 3 seconds. Kept as a plain int (not time.Duration) for env-binding simplicity. |
| `runner.executor.k8s.cleanup_grace_seconds` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_K8S_CLEANUP_GRACE_SECONDS` | integer<br />Default: `30` | Grace period when deleting Pods. Defaults to 30s. |
| `runner.executor.docker.host` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_DOCKER_HOST` | string | Docker daemon URL. Supports unix://, tcp:// and npipe:// schemes. When empty the standard environment (DOCKER_HOST) and the platform default socket are used. |
| `runner.executor.docker.tls_verify` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY` | boolean | Enables TLS certificate verification for tcp:// connections. |
| `runner.executor.docker.cert_path` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_DOCKER_CERT_PATH` | string | Directory holding ca.pem, cert.pem and key.pem for mutual TLS against a remote daemon. |
| `runner.executor.docker.image` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_DOCKER_IMAGE` | string<br />Default: `impishmd/jeh:latest-job` | Default image used for the build container of each task. |
| `runner.executor.docker.helper_image` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_DOCKER_HELPER_IMAGE` | string<br />Default: `impishmd/jeh:latest-helper` | Image used for the transient git-clone container. |
| `runner.executor.docker.network` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_DOCKER_NETWORK` | string<br />Default: `bridge` | Docker network the build container joins. Defaults to "bridge". |
| `runner.executor.docker.pull_policy` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_DOCKER_PULL_POLICY` | string<br />Default: `if-not-present` | Controls image pulling: always, if-not-present or never. |
| `runner.executor.docker.cpu_limit` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_DOCKER_CPU_LIMIT` | number | CPULimit, when > 0, caps the build container CPU (passed as --cpus). |
| `runner.executor.docker.memory_limit` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_DOCKER_MEMORY_LIMIT` | string | MemoryLimit, when non-empty, caps the build container memory (e.g. "2g"). |
| `runner.executor.docker.poll_interval_seconds` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_DOCKER_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | integer<br />Default: `2` | Controls how often container status is polled. Defaults to 2s. |
| `runner.executor.docker.cleanup_grace_seconds` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_DOCKER_CLEANUP_GRACE_SECONDS` | integer<br />Default: `30` | Timeout passed to docker stop. Defaults to 30s. |
| `runner.executor.docker.privileged` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_RUNNER_DOCKER_PRIVILEGED` | boolean | Runs the build container with --privileged. Dangerous; off by default. |
| `runners.offline_timeout_sec`<br />`JEH_RUNNERS_OFFLINE_TIMEOUT_SEC` | integer<br />Default: `120` | Heartbeat staleness after which a runner is considered offline: it receives no new tasks and its "starting" tasks are reassigned to another runner. Must be comfortably larger than the runner poll interval (a few multiples) so a healthy-but-slow runner is never marked offline. |
| `runners.task_fail_timeout_sec`<br />`JEH_RUNNERS_TASK_FAIL_TIMEOUT_SEC` | integer<br />Default: `420` | Heartbeat staleness after which a runner's "running" tasks are failed. Between OfflineTimeoutSec and this value a running task is deliberately left alone: an offline runner may still be executing its jobs and resumes reporting if it reconnects in time. Values below OfflineTimeoutSec are clamped to it. |
| `runners.reconcile_interval_sec`<br />`JEH_RUNNERS_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SEC` | integer<br />Default: `30` | How often the server scans dispatched tasks against runner liveness. |
| `runners.registration_token`<br />`JEH_RUNNER_REGISTRATION_TOKEN` | string | RunnerRegistrationToken is deprecated, use Runners field instead of it. |
| `runners.default_global_runners_mode`<br />`JEH_DEFAULT_GLOBAL_RUNNERS_MODE` | string | What projects do with global runners by default: empty leaves the choice to each project, `disable` excludes them, `prefer` uses them ahead of project runners, `require` allows only them. |

<a id="task-jwt"></a>

## Task JWT

Short-lived tokens that identify a task to external systems. See [Task JWTs](../configuration.md).

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `jwt.enabled`<br />`JEH_JWT_ENABLED` | boolean | When enabled, JEH mints a short-lived JWT for each task run and exposes its public key via `/.well-known/jwks.json`. |
| `jwt.issuer`<br />`JEH_JWT_ISSUER` | string | Value emitted in the `iss` claim of issued JWTs. |
| `jwt.default_ttl`<br />`JEH_JWT_DEFAULT_TTL` | string<br />Default: `1h` | Default lifetime of an issued task JWT, as a Go duration (e.g. `30m`, `1h`). Default: 1h |
| `jwt.max_ttl`<br />`JEH_JWT_MAX_TTL` | string<br />Default: `24h` | Hard upper bound on per-template JWT TTL, as a Go duration. Default: 24h |

<a id="notifications"></a>

## Notifications

Delivery channels for alerts. See [Notifications](../configuration.md).

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `email_alert`<br />`JEH_EMAIL_ALERT` | boolean | Enables the e-mail notification channel. The email_* settings below describe the SMTP server it sends through. |
| `email_sender`<br />`JEH_EMAIL_SENDER` | string | Email address of the sender. |
| `email_host`<br />`JEH_EMAIL_HOST` | string | SMTP server hostname. |
| `email_port`<br />`JEH_EMAIL_PORT` | string | SMTP server port. |
| `email_username`<br />`JEH_EMAIL_USERNAME` | string | Username for SMTP server authentication. |
| `email_password`<br />`JEH_EMAIL_PASSWORD` | string | Password used to authenticate against the SMTP server. Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |
| `email_secure`<br />`JEH_EMAIL_SECURE` | boolean | Enable StartTLS to upgrade an unencrypted SMTP connection to a secure, encrypted one. |
| `email_tls`<br />`JEH_EMAIL_TLS` | boolean | Use SSL or TLS connection for communication with the SMTP server. |
| `email_tls_min_version`<br />`JEH_EMAIL_TLS_MIN_VERSION` | string<br />Default: `1.2` | Minimum TLS version to use for the connection. |
| `telegram_alert`<br />`JEH_TELEGRAM_ALERT` | boolean | Enables the Telegram notification channel, which also needs telegram_token and a default telegram_chat. |
| `telegram_chat`<br />`JEH_TELEGRAM_CHAT` | string | Set to the Chat ID for the chat to send alerts to. Read more in [Telegram Notifications Setup](../configuration.md) |
| `telegram_token`<br />`JEH_TELEGRAM_TOKEN` | string | Bot token issued by BotFather. Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |
| `slack_alert`<br />`JEH_SLACK_ALERT` | boolean | Set to True to enable pushing alerts to slack. It should be used in combination with `slack_url` |
| `slack_url`<br />`JEH_SLACK_URL` | string | The slack webhook url. JEH will used it to POST Slack formatted json alerts to the provided url. |
| `rocketchat_alert`<br />`JEH_ROCKETCHAT_ALERT` | boolean | Set to True to enable pushing alerts to Rocket.Chat. It should be used in combination with `rocketchat_url`. Available since v2.9.56. |
| `rocketchat_url`<br />`JEH_ROCKETCHAT_URL` | string | The rocketchat webhook url. JEH will used it to POST Rocket.Chat formatted json alerts to the provided url. Available since v2.9.56. |
| `microsoft_teams_alert`<br />`JEH_MICROSOFT_TEAMS_ALERT` | boolean | Flag which enables Microsoft Teams alerts. |
| `microsoft_teams_url`<br />`JEH_MICROSOFT_TEAMS_URL` | string | Microsoft Teams webhook URL. |
| `dingtalk_alert`<br />`JEH_DINGTALK_ALERT` | boolean | Enable Dingtalk alerts. |
| `dingtalk_url`<br />`JEH_DINGTALK_URL` | string | Dingtalk messenger webhook URL. |
| `gotify_alert`<br />`JEH_GOTIFY_ALERT` | boolean | Enable Gotify alerts. |
| `gotify_url`<br />`JEH_GOTIFY_URL` | string | Gotify server URL. |
| `gotify_token`<br />`JEH_GOTIFY_TOKEN` | string | Application token issued by the Gotify server. Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |

<a id="logging-and-metrics"></a>

## Logging and metrics

Where server, event, and task logs go, and the Prometheus endpoint. See [Logs](../configuration.md) and [Metrics](../configuration.md).

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `syslog.enabled` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_SYSLOG_ENABLED` | boolean | Enable or disable writing logs to the configured syslog server. |
| `syslog.network` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_SYSLOG_NETWORK` | string | Protocol used to connect to the Syslog server: `udp` or `tcp`. |
| `syslog.address` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_SYSLOG_ADDRESS` | string | Hostname and port of the Syslog server. Example: `localhost:514`. |
| `syslog.tag` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_SYSLOG_TAG` | string | The tag used to mark Job Executor Hub records on the Syslog server. |
| `syslog.format` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_SYSLOG_FORMAT` | string | Format of the Syslog messages. Can be `rfc5424` or empty for default. |
| `metrics.enabled`<br />`JEH_METRICS_ENABLED` | boolean | Serve the Prometheus metrics endpoint. See [Metrics](../configuration.md). |
| `metrics.username`<br />`JEH_METRICS_USERNAME` | string | Username for HTTP basic auth on the metrics endpoint. Leave empty to serve it unauthenticated. |
| `metrics.password`<br />`JEH_METRICS_PASSWORD` | string | Password for HTTP basic auth on the metrics endpoint. Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |
| `log.events.format` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_EVENT_LOG_FORMAT` | string | Event log format. Can be `json` or empty for text. |
| `log.events.enabled` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_EVENT_LOG_ENABLED` | boolean | Enable or disable event logging. |
| `log.events.logger` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_EVENT_LOGGER` | object | JSON map which contains event logger configuration. |
| `log.tasks.enabled` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_TASK_LOG_ENABLED` | boolean | Enable or disable task logging. |
| `log.tasks.format` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_TASK_LOG_FORMAT` | string | Task log format. Can be `json` or empty for text. |
| `log.tasks.logger` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_TASK_LOGGER` | object | JSON map which contains task logger configuration. |
| `log.tasks.result_logger` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_TASK_RESULT_LOGGER` | object | JSON map which contains task result logger configuration. |

<a id="teams-and-invitations"></a>

## Teams and invitations

How people are added to projects. See [Teams](../configuration.md).

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `teams.invites_enabled`<br />`JEH_TEAMS_INVITES_ENABLED` | boolean | Allow users to invite members to teams. |
| `teams.invite_type`<br />`JEH_TEAMS_INVITE_TYPE` | string<br />Default: `username` | Type of invite: `username` (default), `email`, `both`. |
| `teams.members_can_leave`<br />`JEH_TEAMS_MEMBERS_CAN_LEAVE` | boolean | Allow members to leave teams. |

<a id="subscription"></a>

## Subscription

Upstream subscription interface options. Proprietary implementations are not included in JEH. See [feature scope](../configuration.md#feature-scope).

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `subscription.key`<br />`JEH_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY` | string | Subscription key or token that can be set via config. When this is set, subscription activation from the web interface is disabled. Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |
| `subscription.key_file`<br />`JEH_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY_FILE` | string | Path to subscription key or token file. |
| `subscription.server_url`<br />`JEH_SUBSCRIPTION_SERVER_URL` | string | Upstream subscription interface URL. Unset in JEH; proprietary implementations are not included. |

<a id="high-availability"></a>

## High availability

Running several nodes against one database. See [High availability](../configuration.md).

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ha.enabled` **upstream Enterprise**<br />`JEH_HA_ENABLED` | boolean | Enable High Availability (HA) mode. |
| `ha.node_id` **upstream Enterprise**<br />`JEH_HA_NODE_ID` | string | auto-generated if empty |
| `ha.redis.addr` **upstream Enterprise**<br />`JEH_HA_REDIS_ADDR` | string | Address of the Redis server used for HA. Example: `localhost:6379`. |
| `ha.redis.db` **upstream Enterprise**<br />`JEH_HA_REDIS_DB` | integer | Redis database number. |
| `ha.redis.pass` **upstream Enterprise**<br />`JEH_HA_REDIS_PASS` | string | Password for the Redis server. Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |
| `ha.redis.user` **upstream Enterprise**<br />`JEH_HA_REDIS_USER` | string | Username for the Redis server. |
| `ha.redis.tls` **upstream Enterprise**<br />`JEH_HA_REDIS_TLS` | boolean | Enable TLS for the Redis connection. |
| `ha.redis.tls_skip_verify` **upstream Enterprise**<br />`JEH_HA_REDIS_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY` | boolean | Skip TLS certificate verification for the Redis connection. |

<a id="audit-log"></a>

## Audit log

Recording who did what in JEH, and sending the events to a SIEM. See [Audit log](../configuration.md).

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `audit.enabled`<br />`JEH_AUDIT_ENABLED` | boolean | Turns on the audit log. |
| `audit.instance_id`<br />`JEH_AUDIT_INSTANCE_ID` | string | Installation name added to every event. Required when enabled. |
| `audit.trusted_proxy_cidrs`<br />`JEH_AUDIT_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` | array | Lists the proxy networks allowed to pass the client address. |
| `audit.retention_days`<br />`JEH_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS` | integer | Deletes audit events older than this many days. 0 keeps everything. |
| `audit.syslog.id` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_AUDIT_SYSLOG_ID` | string | Names the destination. Keep it when the address changes. |
| `audit.syslog.address` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_AUDIT_SYSLOG_ADDRESS` | string | Receiver host and port. |
| `audit.syslog.timeout` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_AUDIT_SYSLOG_TIMEOUT` | string<br />Default: `10s` | Limits connecting to the receiver and sending events. |
| `audit.syslog.ca_file` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_AUDIT_SYSLOG_CA_FILE` | string | PEM file with extra CA certificates to trust. |
| `audit.syslog.server_name` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_AUDIT_SYSLOG_SERVER_NAME` | string | Name to check in the receiver certificate. |
| `audit.splunk_hec.id` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_AUDIT_SPLUNK_HEC_ID` | string | Names the destination. Keep it when the URL changes. A new ID starts with new events. |
| `audit.splunk_hec.url` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_AUDIT_SPLUNK_HEC_URL` | string | Full HEC endpoint, for example https://hec.example:8088/services/collector/event. |
| `audit.splunk_hec.token` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_AUDIT_SPLUNK_HEC_TOKEN` | string | HEC token sent as "Authorization: Splunk \<token>". Secret: keep it out of shell history and version control. |
| `audit.splunk_hec.index` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_AUDIT_SPLUNK_HEC_INDEX` | string | Target index. Empty uses the default index of the token. |
| `audit.splunk_hec.source` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_AUDIT_SPLUNK_HEC_SOURCE` | string<br />Default: `jeh` | HEC source of every event. |
| `audit.splunk_hec.sourcetype` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_AUDIT_SPLUNK_HEC_SOURCETYPE` | string<br />Default: `jeh:audit` | HEC sourcetype of every event. |
| `audit.splunk_hec.timeout` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_AUDIT_SPLUNK_HEC_TIMEOUT` | string<br />Default: `10s` | Bounds one HTTP request with one batch of events. |
| `audit.splunk_hec.ca_file` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_AUDIT_SPLUNK_HEC_CA_FILE` | string | PEM bundle added to the system roots. |
| `audit.splunk_hec.server_name` **upstream Pro**<br />`JEH_AUDIT_SPLUNK_HEC_SERVER_NAME` | string | Overrides the name checked in the receiver certificate. |

<a id="debugging"></a>

## Debugging

Switches useful when diagnosing a problem. Do not leave them on in production.

| Option / Environment variable | Type / Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `debugging.api_delay`<br />`JEH_API_DELAY` | string | Add delay to API responses (for debugging purposes). |
| `debugging.pprof_dump_dir`<br />`JEH_PPROF_DUMP_DIR` | string | Directory for pprof dump files. |
